svg.title: Semantic scaffolding design atlas
svg.desc: Eighteen illustrated relations connect task meaning with the human contribution an interface enables or invites. Representations may be constructed by AI, people or both. Form and access, help timing, and social conditions can vary across relations. These are conceptual schematics, not measured activities or learning outcomes.

text.tspan: Read the task meaning and the person's contribution together.

g.title: Which aspect of the system is made inspectable?
How can a result be traced or checked?
How is content condensed, interpreted or recast?
Through which form can a person perceive meaning?
Which relationships give material its structure?
What is placed in a common comparison frame?
How is relevant material found and brought into view?
What is kept available for continuing the work?
How does a person specify what the system should do?
Where can a person intervene in the work?
How are possibilities offered and shaped?
What can be tried before acting in the real setting?
What helps a person decide where to look or what to do?
What basis is provided for judging the work?
What help is available, and when is it available?
How are stages, responsibilities and continuity arranged?
Which part of a person's thinking is elicited?
How do contributions and viewpoints become shared?

text.tspan: Representations may be constructed by AI, people or both. Activities shown are design possibilities.
